references.text: The priest takes a handful of the grain offering and brings it to the altar, describing the same process of bringing the offering to the priest.
The law concerning the grain offering describes how it is to be brought before the Lord's presence, in front of the altar.
Describes how the offering is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting before the Lord's presence.
Every grain offering baked in an oven or made in a pan shall belong to the priest who presents it.
Grain offerings and drink offerings are to be brought before the Lord's presence at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Whoever brings an offering to the Lord must also bring a grain offering.
Every high priest is appointed to present gifts and sacrifices to God, paralleling the priest's role in receiving the grain offering.
Both verses illustrate the crucial role the priest plays in bringing the grain offering from the offerer to the altar for the completion of atonement.
Lev 6:14 elaborates on how the grain offering is to be prepared and physically presented before being brought forward as described in Lev 2:8.
Lev 2:1 and 2:8 form a logical whole where the first defines the content of the offering and the second instructs on its presentation.
Lev 5:13 explicitly refers to the rules in Lev 2 (the grain offering) to determine how the remainder of the offering is to be distributed.
